facts.statement: The only known fossils of Ilerdopteryx viai are a set of isolated contour feathers.
facts.quote: The type species, I. viai, is known only from a collection of isolated contour feathers.

facts.statement: Ilerdopteryx lived in the Lower Cretaceous of Spain within the La Pedrera de Rúbies Formation.
facts.quote: Ilerdopteryx is an extinct genus of birds, perhaps an enantiornithine, from the Lower Cretaceous La Pedrera de Rúbies Formation lithographic limestone of Spain.

facts.statement: Ilerdopteryx is classified as a bird, possibly belonging to the Enantiornithes group.
facts.quote: Ilerdopteryx is an extinct genus of birds, perhaps an enantiornithine

facts.statement: The parent group of Ilerdopteryx is the Archaeornithes.
Ilerdopteryx lived during the Barremian stage, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of the genus Ilerdopteryx.
The genus Ilerdopteryx was named by Lacasa-Ruiz in 1985.
The species Ilerdopteryx viai was described by Lacasa-Ruiz in 1985.

rejected.statement: Ilerdopteryx belongs to the class Aves.
